reason: Rain on the ground should collect in hollows before flowing into lower terrain.
expectation: Water will gather in the hollows.

effect: The rain has collected into pools; the slope may carry their water toward the basin.
reaction: The small pools are a satisfying first step toward a sea.
reason: A slope toward the basin suggests a route for the pooled water to flow downhill.

choice.with: A slope toward a broad basin

expectation: The pooled water will flow toward the basin.

effect: The pools overflowed into runoff toward the basin; I need to find its next available connection.
reaction: The connection between separate pools is a clear progression.
reason: The runoff is heading toward the sea, but no separate basin item is visible, so checking its partners should clarify the next step.
expectation: The inspection will reveal how the runoff can gather or move through the rock.

effect: Runoff can combine with either the hollows or the cracked crust, offering routes toward both goals.
reaction: The two partners make the next choices clearer.
reason: Hollows can collect the runoff in low ground, advancing the sea goal.
expectation: The runoff will gather into a larger body of water.

alternatives.reason: The cracks may provide the route through the rock.

effect: The runoff accumulated into an early sea, completing the first goal; the cracked crust remains a promising route through the rock.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the separate pools become a sea.
reason: The inspection showed that runoff can combine with the cracked crust, which suggests water can enter the rock.
expectation: Water will flow into cracks in the volcanic crust.

effect: Runoff has entered fractures in the crust; the less permeable layer may determine where it goes next.
reaction: The hidden groundwater route is a useful contrast with surface runoff.
reason: A less permeable layer could slow water moving through the fractured rock.
expectation: Water will collect or flow along the less permeable layer.

effect: The less permeable layer diverted groundwater sideways; I need to find where that flow can go next.
reaction: The way permeability redirects water is a useful detail.
reason: The groundwater's next connection is not obvious from the remaining visible items, so inspecting it should clarify the route.
expectation: The inspection will reveal what the diverted groundwater can interact with next.

effect: The diverted groundwater emerged as a spring on the slope, completing the route through the rock and the chapter.
reaction: The spring neatly connects the hidden groundwater route back to the surface.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following water through fractured rock, along a less permeable layer and out as a spring made groundwater flow understandable as a connected process.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the runoff was useful, but the partner list alone was less illuminating than seeing what the combinations did.

surprise.text: I had not anticipated that the diverted groundwater would reappear as a spring above the shore.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the slope connection became clear when the groundwater emerged there.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in another chapter if it similarly connected familiar features to physical processes, though the straightforward sequence left relatively few difficult choices.
